# Verdict: REVISE ## Summary The `AppLayout` component introduces severe focus order and focus visibility defects that undermine its semantic HTML structure. While basic landmarks, headings, and a skip link are present, the interaction design fails real keyboard and assistive technology users due to four primary flaws: 1. **Positive `tabIndex={1}` on the Floating Action Button (FAB)** hijacks the initial page focus, placing the user at the bottom-right corner and bypassing the skip link and top navigation. 2. **Visual vs. DOM order disconnection via CSS `order: -1`** forces focus to jump over the sidebar into the main content, tab through all content links, and only then jump back up and left into the primary sidebar navigation. 3. **Sub-threshold focus indicator contrast on sidebar navigation links (`1.56:1`)** renders focus effectively invisible on `#f8fafc` background. 4. **Non-focusable skip link target (`
`)** lacks `tabIndex={-1}`, causing focus transfer to fail in modern browsers. --- ## Pre-commitment Predictions Before auditing the code, common design pitfalls for this component layout were predicted: - **Prediction 1**: Disconnection between visual reading order and DOM sequence caused by CSS flexbox `order` or positioning. (*Confirmed*: `.sidebar` uses `order: -1` while DOM places `
` before `
`.) - **Prediction 2**: Improper positive `tabindex` on persistent floating UI controls. (*Confirmed*: FAB uses `tabIndex={1}`.) - **Prediction 3**: Skip link target missing `tabindex="-1"`, preventing keyboard focus from advancing to main content. (*Confirmed*: `
` lacks `tabindex`.) - **Prediction 4**: Insufficient focus indicator contrast on tinted sidebar backgrounds. (*Confirmed*: `#a8d0f0` on `#f8fafc` measures `1.56:1` contrast.) - **Prediction 5**: Landmark labels naming visual location rather than functional intent. (*Confirmed*: "Sidebar navigation" and "Header navigation".) --- ## Findings ### Critical Findings #### 1. Positive `tabIndex={1}` on FAB Hijacks Initial Sequential Focus Order - **Location**: `AppLayout.jsx:79` (`tabIndex={1}`) - **User Group Impacted**: Keyboard-only users, screen reader users - **WCAG / APG Citation**: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A), WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A) - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: In HTML/DOM focus navigation, any positive integer `tabindex` (`tabindex > 0`) is elevated into a priority focus set that receives focus *before* all default (`tabindex="0"`) elements. On initial page load, the very first `Tab` keystroke jumps straight to the FAB at the bottom-right corner (`x: right, y: bottom`), bypassing the skip link, the application header, and the main navigation. This disorients keyboard users and breaks sequential navigation. - **Fix**: Remove `tabIndex={1}`. The accessible name is `"Create new report"`, which does not contain the visual string `"+"` or `"plus"`. A speech-input user saying "Click Plus" cannot activate the button. - **Fix**: Wrap the symbol in `+`, provide an accessible tooltip, or include `"Create Report"` as visible text. 2. **Skip Link Focus Outline Contrast is Borderline (`2.83:1`)**: - **Location**: `AppLayout.css:19` (`outline: 2px solid #2563eb;`) - **Evidence**: Focused skip link sits on header background `#1e293b`. - **WCAG**: WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (Level AA), WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (Level AA). - **Detail**: `#2563eb` against `#1e293b` yields a contrast ratio of `2.83:1`, which fails the `3:1` threshold against its dark background. - **Fix**: Use a lighter outline color on dark surfaces, such as `#60a5fa` (which is already used for header links at `>6:1`). 3. **Landmark Labels Use Visual Position Instead of Functional Purpose**: - **Location**: `AppLayout.jsx:15` (`aria-label="Header navigation"`), `AppLayout.jsx:62` (`aria-label="Sidebar navigation"`) - **WCAG**: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A), WAI-ARIA APG Landmark Practices. - **Detail**: Labels like "Header navigation" and "Sidebar navigation" describe screen coordinates rather than semantic roles. Screen reader users navigating landmark lists need functional distinction. - **Fix**: Change to `aria-label="Utility"` / `aria-label="User"` for the header nav, and `aria-label="Primary"` / `aria-label="Main"` for the sidebar nav. --- ### Enhancements 1. **Missing `aria-current="page"` on Active Navigation Link**: - In `AppLayout.jsx:65`, `Dashboard` matches the active page (`

Dashboard

`). Adding `aria-current="page"` informs assistive technology which item in the navigation represents the current location (WCAG 4.1.2). 2. **Semantics of `
` for Primary Site Navigation**: - In `AppLayout.jsx:61`, wrapping primary site navigation in `
` semantically marks it as tangential/supplementary. Primary navigation belongs in a standard container or `
` without `
`. --- ## What's Missing 1. **Missing Focus Receiver on Skip Link Target**: No `tabIndex={-1}` on `
` or the destination heading. 2. **Missing Active State Indicator**: No programmatic indication (`aria-current="page"`) for screen readers to identify the current page in navigation. 3. **Missing Tooltip / Accessible Name Parity**: No visible label or tooltip on the floating button explaining what `+` does before activation. 4. **Missing Content Obscurity Safeguards**: At `200%` or `400%` zoom, fixed position `.fab` (`bottom: 24px, right: 24px`) can overlay content without responsive positioning or `scroll-padding-bottom` (WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured). --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes - **Screen reader user**: Heading structure is clean (H1 → H2), but `
` misleadingly marks primary navigation as auxiliary. When reading linearly or navigating landmarks, the sidebar navigation appears after all main content tasks and reports. - **Keyboard-only user**: Experience is broken. Pressing `Tab` immediately jumps to the FAB at the bottom right. Tabbing through the page causes erratic focus jumping between header, main body, and sidebar. The skip link fails to anchor keyboard focus, and focus outlines inside the sidebar disappear against the background. - **Low vision user (200% zoom, high contrast)**: Sidebar focus indicator (`#a8d0f0` on `#f8fafc`) is completely washed out (`1.56:1`). Fixed FAB risks obscuring bottom task rows. - **Cognitive accessibility**: Focus jumping from the top right to the bottom right, then back to the top left, and then bouncing between columns violates spatial predictability and causes disorientation. --- ## Perspective Alarm Levels | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |-------------|:-----------:|----------------| | **Screen reader** | **MEDIUM** | Auxiliary landmark used for primary nav; missing `aria-current="page"`; out-of-order reading sequence. | | **Keyboard-only** | **HIGH** | `tabIndex={1}` priority hijacking; `order: -1` visual/DOM mismatch; broken skip target. | | **Low vision** | **HIGH** | `1.56:1` focus indicator contrast failure on sidebar; fixed FAB content obstruction. | | **Cognitive** | **HIGH** | Erratic, non-sequential focus movement across multiple screen axes. | | **Vestibular & motion** | **LOW** | No animated transitions, carousels, or parallax effects present. | | **Auditory access** | **LOW** | No audio or video media present in layout. | | **Environmental contrast** | **HIGH** | Sub-3:1 focus ring contrast on sidebar (`1.56:1`) and skip link (`2.83:1`). | --- ## Verdict Justification - **Why REVISE**: The component uses valid HTML5 semantic tags and clean heading hierarchy, and automated syntax checks pass. However, shipping with `tabIndex={1}` and `order: -1` creates severe, disorienting focus order defects that fail WCAG 2.4.3 (Level A) and WCAG 2.4.13 (Level AA). - **Upgrade Path to ACCEPT**: 1. Remove `tabIndex={1}` from `.fab`. 2. Swap the DOM sequence in `AppLayout.jsx` so `
` precedes `
`, and delete `.sidebar { order: -1; }` in `AppLayout.css`. 3. Replace `.sidebar-nav a:focus { outline: 2px solid #a8d0f0; }` with a high-contrast outline (`#2563eb`, `5.2:1`). 4. Attach `id="content"` and `tabIndex={-1}` directly to `
`. --- ## Open Questions (Unscored) 1. *Is the Floating Action Button intended to be present on every page or dashboard-specific?* If persistent, consider placing it in a landmarked toolbar (`
` or within `
`). 2. *Should the FAB expand into a menu or trigger a modal?* If it triggers a dialog or menu, it will require `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`.
